subject.title: Feature: Silence Watchdog + Response Delivery Confirmation — runtime-enforced operator visibility

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-on gateway runtime contract for active-turn silence beacons and final-response delivery confirmation, and if so what defaults, config shape, and channel-visible alert semantics should it use?
rationale: The requested behavior adds user-visible messages, retry/alert policy, and new configuration across channel delivery and active-turn state, which cannot be safely chosen from code inspection alone.

options.title: Design one shared contract
options.body: Define a single maintainer-approved runtime contract that reuses existing durable delivery and heartbeat/typing infrastructure for beacons, confirmation, retry, and alert semantics.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical items
options.body: Let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77771, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87561, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46830 carry their separate slices and close this umbrella only after maintainers confirm the split is complete.

options.title: Decline default-on operator messages
options.body: Keep existing heartbeat, typing, pending-final, and durable delivery behavior without adding default-on beacon or no-response alert surfaces.

recommendation.title: Design one shared contract
recommendation.body: Define a single maintainer-approved runtime contract that reuses existing durable delivery and heartbeat/typing infrastructure for beacons, confirmation, retry, and alert semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest shared history trail for typing lifecycle and channel/message delivery foundations points here.
